knowledge-base.overview: Flutter 3.x guardrails, widget composition, Riverpod state management, go_router navigation, Material 3 theming, clean architecture data layer, and testing. Applies to iOS, Android, Web, and Desktop apps sharing a single Dart codebase. Use Riverpod as the primary state solution; go_router for all navigation; freezed for immutable models.

core-principles.principle: Build complex UIs by composing small, focused widgets. A build method over 50 lines is a signal to extract sub-widgets.
Describe what the UI should look like; Flutter handles all rendering. Never manipulate the widget tree imperatively.
Widgets are configuration objects — immutable snapshots. Mutable state lives in State classes or Riverpod providers.
Riverpod is the single state management solution. No Provider package, no GetX, no BLoC unless an existing codebase already uses them.
Default to Material 3 with useMaterial3: true and ColorScheme.fromSeed. Never customize theme by overriding individual widget styles directly.

guardrail.rule: Wrap the app root in ProviderScope. Without it, all Riverpod providers throw ProviderNotFoundException at runtime.
Use ref.watch() only in build methods and provider bodies. Use ref.read() in callbacks, event handlers, and initState. Calling ref.watch() outside build causes runtime errors.
guardrail.bad: ElevatedButton( onPressed: () => ref.watch(counterProvider), // BLOCKER child: const Text('Tap'), )

guardrail.rule: Dispose TextEditingController, AnimationController, ScrollController, and all subscriptions in dispose(). Memory leaks from undisposed controllers accumulate silently.
Never perform async work directly in build(). Use providers or FutureBuilder. Async calls in build() fire on every rebuild and cause race conditions.
guardrail.good: final usersAsync = ref.watch(usersProvider); // AsyncNotifierProvider handles the future

guardrail.rule: Keep build methods under 50 lines. Extract sub-widgets into separate classes (not private methods) so Flutter can optimize rebuilds.
Always use super.key in widget constructors. Missing key causes Flutter to silently reuse widget state across list items.
Use named routes with context.goNamed() / context.pushNamed() — never hardcode path strings at call sites.
Define an errorBuilder on GoRouter for unknown routes. Unhandled route errors produce blank screens without it.
Use const constructors for all stateless widgets where possible. const prevents unnecessary rebuilds.
Use ref.listen() for side effects — snackbars, dialogs, navigation triggered by state changes. Never perform side effects inside build().
Store sensitive credentials (tokens, API keys) with flutter_secure_storage, not shared_preferences. shared_preferences is plaintext on device.
Run dart run build_runner build after any change to @freezed, @JsonSerializable, or @riverpod annotations. Generated files (.g.dart, .freezed.dart) must stay in sync.
